item: process_owner: a wall-clock step no longer turns a live owner into dead (gate item 41, R261)
summary: On Linux the owner record carries boot-relative start ticks, the kernel boot id and the pid-namespace inode. Same boot compares ticks, so an NTP step, date -s or VM resume no longer makes a live lease holder, rollup build or backup staging owner look dead. A different boot id is dead, a different pid namespace or any unreadable piece is unknown (fail closed). Records without the fields, macOS and Windows keep the psutil comparison and stay exposed to a step. Limit: a restarted container (new pid namespace) leaves its predecessor unknown, so a leftover lease stays until deleted by hand (item 27).
